56. **Sign-up and email verification built (2026-11-23, M1 part 2a).** The `signUp`, `resendEmailVerification` and `confirmEmail` rows of §13.3 are built and leave `x-pending-operations` for `paths` in `openapi.yaml`; §9.1's `signup_ip` and `verify_resend` rows joined `RATE_LIMITS`. Decisions where the rows were short or disagreed with another document: (a) the bodies follow §3.4's envelope, `{data: {status: …}}`, which the rows had shortened to the inner object; (b) `confirmEmail` said "`token` expired or used"; [02 AC-J04-06](02-user-journeys-and-acceptance-criteria.md#j-04-sign-up--verify) and the J-04 concurrency row answer the same link again with 200 "already verified", so any link of an account that is already `active` answers 200 with no write, and an unknown, expired, replaced or other-purpose token answers 422 with the one item code `token_invalid` ([01 AC-FR-IAM-002-4](01-product-requirements.md#fr-iam-002-email-verification-required-for-checkout-and-shop-application) edited to match, 01 note 32); (c) `resendEmailVerification` takes no body, and a signed-in user who is no longer `pending_verification` gets the surface default 403 `FORBIDDEN`; (d) `signUp` inserts `ON CONFLICT (email) DO NOTHING`, whose arbiter is `users_email_key`, so a concurrent signup raises no violation instead of one being caught ([04a §5.1](04a-data-dictionary-tables.md#51-users), 04 note 38). On resending before sign-in, [02 J-04](02-user-journeys-and-acceptance-criteria.md#j-04-sign-up--verify) step 3 put a resend button on `/verify-email` right after `signUp`, which creates no session, while this row keeps resend behind a session; the tech lead ruled the same day that this row stands and the page asks the user to sign in for a new link ([risks §2.3](risks-and-open-decisions.md#23-decision-log), 02 note 27). After the Fable review (2026-11-23): the `signUp` row names the statement that runs, `ON CONFLICT (email) DO NOTHING` with `users_email_key` as its arbiter; `full_name` is normalised to NFC before its length is checked, in code points, because NFC can lengthen Devanagari and the column's CHECK would otherwise answer 500 ([04 §2.8](04-domain-model-and-data-dictionary.md#28-text-normalisation-and-lengths)); `age_confirmed` accepts the JSON `true` only; and `confirmEmail`'s errors name the validator's own items for a missing, non-string or over-long `token`, and `token_invalid` for a suspended or deactivated account's link. Whether verification must also prove the password is [Open OD-62](risks-and-open-decisions.md#22-decision-table).
57. **Sign-in and sign-out built (2026-11-23, M1 part 3).** The `logIn`, `logOut` and `getMe` rows of §13.3 are built and leave `x-pending-operations` for `paths` in `openapi.yaml` (its note 48); §4.1 and §9.1 say how. Decisions where the rows were short or silent: (a) `logIn`'s 200 follows §3.4's envelope, `{data: {user, redirect_to}}`, with `user` the shared `user` prop's members plus `status`; (b) the `guest` middleware answers `/api/v1` with 409 `CONFLICT` "You are already signed in" and a page with a 302 to `/` that no longer forwards the visited query ([07 TM-14](07-security-threat-model-and-permissions.md#tm-14-unsafe-redirects-and-return-urls), [09 §3.4](09-code-structure-and-engineering-standards.md#34-middleware) row 3); (c) the row was silent on staff before the TOTP challenge exists (part 5): a staff member's password sign-in answers as a customer's, with no extra session key, and because the session holds no `mfa_verified_at` the admin surface answers 401 `MFA_REQUIRED` (§4.3) and its pages redirect to `/mfa`, which part 5 builds; 02 J-04 step 6 ("sent to `/mfa` next") holds through that redirect, and in development the development sign-in stays the way into the admin pages ([07 §3.13](07-security-threat-model-and-permissions.md#313-development-only-sign-in)); (d) the status check runs inside the limiter's check, so a suspended or deactivated account keeps its `login_acct_ip` point, and the success that deletes the key is a sign-in; (e) a request a login limiter refuses writes no `auth.login_failed` row ([04 note 39](04-domain-model-and-data-dictionary.md#consistency-notes-for-editor)); (f) `getMe` names its members: the consents as booleans, as `updateMe` takes them, the role of an unrevoked `platform_staff` row whether or not TOTP is enrolled, and the shops the user owns or is an `active` member of as `{slug, name, status, role}`, which the controller reads from the shops module; (g) `return_to` must be a string or null (422 otherwise), and a rejected value becomes `/` as the row says, with a log line that leaves the value out, since it may carry a token. After the Fable review (2026-11-23): the `logIn` row's compare-and-set also requires the `security_stamp` the check read and, on a rehash, the same `password_hash`, and a miss answers 403 or the generic 401 with no session, where the row said it was "on a signed-in status, returning the stamp"; a `return_to` over 2,048 characters becomes `/` ([07 note 50](07-security-threat-model-and-permissions.md#consistency-notes-for-editor)). Tests: `T-IAM-003` and `T-IAM-004` (new) and the sign-in parts of `T-SEC-009`, `T-SEC-011`, `T-SEC-012`, `T-SEC-013`, `T-SEC-017`, `T-SEC-043`, `T-SEC-101` and `T-API-002` ([10 note 76](10-testing-and-quality-gates.md#consistency-notes-for-editor)).
58. **Password reset and change, and revoking sessions, built (2026-11-23, M1 part 4).** The `requestPasswordReset`, `resetPassword`, `changePassword` and `revokeAllSessions` rows of §13.3 are built and leave `x-pending-operations` for `paths` in `openapi.yaml`; §9.1's `pwreset_email` and `pwreset_ip` rows joined `RATE_LIMITS`, and the `reauth` row is built for `changePassword` and the courier operations. Decisions where the rows were short or silent: (a) the bodies follow §3.4's envelope: `requestPasswordReset` answers 202 `{data: {status: "reset_email_sent"}}`, `resetPassword` 200 `{data: {status: "password_reset"}}`, `changePassword` 200 `{data: {status: "password_changed"}}` and `revokeAllSessions` 202 `{data: {status: "sessions_revoked"}}`; (b) `requestPasswordReset` and `resetPassword` run without the `guest` middleware, as `signUp` and `confirmEmail` do, because the emailed link may be opened in a browser that is signed in; (c) a 429 from `pwreset_email` says nothing about an account because both limiters are charged before the lookup for every valid request, so "202 either way" in §9.1 means the answer does not depend on the account, not that the limiter never refuses (AC-J18-01 asks for the 429); (d) `resetPassword` looks the live token up before it hashes the new password, so an unknown or spent token costs no scrypt hash, and answers one `token_invalid` for every refusal, a suspended account's token included, like `confirmEmail`; (e) the `changePassword` and `revokeAllSessions` rows were silent on a concurrent change: both rotate the stamp by a compare-and-set on a signed-in status and the acting session's stamp (and, for a change, the hash the check verified), so a stale session cannot take the new stamp and survive the job, and a miss answers 401 `UNAUTHENTICATED`, or 403 `ACCOUNT_SUSPENDED` after a suspension; (f) a wrong current password adds its `login_acct_ip` point with `increment()` after the check rather than charging it first: `reauth` is the gate of `changePassword`, so a sign-in burst from the same network does not block a password change; (g) the audit actions are `auth.password_reset`, `auth.password_change` and `auth.sessions_revoke`, by the user as `customer`, or as `platform_staff` with the role ([04a §15.3](04a-data-dictionary-tables.md#153-audit_logs), [04 note 40](04-domain-model-and-data-dictionary.md#consistency-notes-for-editor)); `requestPasswordReset` writes none, as its row lists none. Conflicts, settled by the owners: [02 J-18](02-user-journeys-and-acceptance-criteria.md#j-18-password-reset) step 3 marks a `pending_verification` account verified on a reset [Assumption], where [07 §3.12](07-security-threat-model-and-permissions.md#312-user-status-transitions) listed only `confirmEmail` for that transition; the reset proves the mailbox as well as setting the password, so 07 §3.12 gains the row and the `resetPassword` row says so ([07 note 51](07-security-threat-model-and-permissions.md#consistency-notes-for-editor)). [01 AC-FR-NOT-001-1](01-product-requirements.md#fr-not-001-account-emails) lists a "sessions revoked" template that no row of §13.3 sent; after the Fable review it is built and `revokeAllSessions` sends it, because it is the one operation whose whole effect is that, and a stolen session could otherwise sign the holder out everywhere unnoticed; the `reauth` lockout, which signs every device out, sends the same notice. After the Fable review (2026-11-23): `resetPassword` charges the proposed `pwreset_token` limiter (5 per live token per hour) after the lookup and before the hash, so a burst carrying one live token reaches the hasher at most 5 times; §4.2 row 3 gains the guest token routes' exception, so a stale session that opens a reset or verification link is served as a guest instead of being redirected with the token in `return_to` ([07 note 51](07-security-threat-model-and-permissions.md#consistency-notes-for-editor)). In review round 2: a signed-in account, even an unverified one under someone else's address, could queue one email per request through `revokeAllSessions` (no limiter, and the session survives) and through successful `changePassword` calls (`reauth` gives a right password's points back), because `api_user` is not built; §9.1 gains `password_change` and `revoke_all` (5 per hour per user each, proposed), charged before anything is written, and both rows answer `RATE_LIMITED`. Tests: `T-IAM-005`, `T-IAM-006` (new), `T-IAM-105`, `T-IAM-109`, `T-SEC-009`, `T-SEC-010`, `T-SEC-011`, `T-SEC-012`, `T-NOT-101` and `T-API-002` ([10 note 77](10-testing-and-quality-gates.md#consistency-notes-for-editor)).
59. **Staff MFA built (2026-11-23, M1 part 5).** The `verifyMfaChallenge`, `startTotpEnrollment` and `confirmTotpEnrollment` rows of §13.3 are built and leave `x-pending-operations` for `paths` in `openapi.yaml`; §4.3's gates and §9.1's `mfa_user` and `mfa` rows are built. Decisions where the rows were short or silent, each following its owner: (a) the bodies follow §3.4's envelope: `{data: {otpauth_uri, secret}}`, `{data: {status: mfa_enabled}}` and `{data: {redirect_to}}`; (b) in R1 only staff have TOTP ([01 FR-IAM-007](01-product-requirements.md#fr-iam-007-totp-mfa-mandatory-for-platform-staff); owner MFA is R2), so a caller without an unrevoked staff row or an `active` account gets 403 `FORBIDDEN` from all three, before any limiter, and the rows list it; (c) the checks that need no secret come first and charge nothing: a challenge before enrolment and a confirmation without a started enrolment are 409 `CONFLICT`, and a token that is not the caller's live `mfa_enrollment` token is 422 `token_invalid` before the password is hashed, so only a wrong password counts toward `reauth` and only a wrong code toward `mfa_user` and `mfa`, as the `T-SEC-008` row of [07 §4.9](07-security-threat-model-and-permissions.md#49-how-authorization-is-tested) reads; (d) `confirmTotpEnrollment` does not write `mfa_verified_at`, because [07 §3.2](07-security-threat-model-and-permissions.md#32-what-a-session-may-contain) names only `verifyMfaChallenge` and a `totp_code` approval as its writers; it records the code's step, so the page asks for the next code; (e) `logIn` sends an active staff member to `/mfa`, carrying the checked destination as `return_to`, because [01 AC-FR-IAM-007-1](01-product-requirements.md#fr-iam-007-totp-mfa-mandatory-for-platform-staff) and [02 J-04](02-user-journeys-and-acceptance-criteria.md#j-04-sign-up--verify) step 6 send staff to enrolment or the challenge after sign-in, which the row's "`redirect_to` = the validated `return_to`" did not say; (f) the "two-step verification turned on" email of [07 §3.9](07-security-threat-model-and-permissions.md#39-mfa-totp-for-platform-staff) gets its event ID from the consumed token, one email per enrolment window, and its template joins [01 AC-FR-NOT-001-1](01-product-requirements.md#fr-not-001-account-emails) ([01 note 34](01-product-requirements.md#consistency-notes-for-editor)); (g) the audit actions `auth.mfa_enrollment_start`, `auth.mfa_verify`, `auth.mfa_failed` and `platform_staff.mfa_enable` are proposed in [04a §15.3](04a-data-dictionary-tables.md#153-audit_logs), next to the proposed `auth.mfa_locked`. After the Fable review (2026-11-23): the `mfa_user` row and the `verifyMfaChallenge` row say exactly what the limiter does: after 5 wrong codes the next attempt is refused unchecked, right or wrong, and starts the block, the reading [07 §3.9](07-security-threat-model-and-permissions.md#39-mfa-totp-for-platform-staff) and [01 note 35](01-product-requirements.md#consistency-notes-for-editor) record for AC-FR-IAM-007-4; an attempt that fails on a data fault gives its points back; the `mfa` row says when it can act; and `totp_start` (proposed) bounds right-password starts, as `password_change` bounds changes.
60. **The profile and the deletion request built (2026-11-23, M1 part 6a).** The `updateMe` and `requestAccountDeletion` rows of §13.3 are built and leave `x-pending-operations` for `paths` in `openapi.yaml` (its note 51); §9.1's `reauth` row is built for `requestAccountDeletion` too. Decisions where the rows were short or silent, each following its owner: (a) `updateMe`'s "Profile" output is the account as `getMe` answers it, `{data: …}` under §3.4's envelope, and `requestAccountDeletion` answers 202 `{data: {status: "deletion_requested"}}`; (b) every `updateMe` member is optional, `phone: null` removes the number (all three columns, `users_phone_parts_check`), and `email` is an unknown member, because [11 §14.6](11-deployment-and-operations.md#146-recovery-procedures-that-need-host-access) says no R1 operation changes the login email; (c) neither is ⟳, because `users` has no `version` ([04 §2.10](04-domain-model-and-data-dictionary.md#210-optimistic-concurrency) does not list it), nor ⚷ (§7.7); both guard their write with a compare-and-set on what the account check and the row lock read, a signed-in status and the acting session's stamp, and `requestAccountDeletion` also the hash the password check verified, so a stale session never writes over a suspension, a password change or "sign out everywhere" (401 or 403, as for `changePassword`); (d) the consent audit row is one `user.consent_change` per request that grants or withdraws, with `granted` and `withdrawn` naming the columns and the source `account_page` (AC-FR-IAM-013-4), and none for the name or the phone, which the row named "Audit for consent changes" only; a repeated `true` keeps the first opt-in time; (e) as first built, the deletion request took an optional free-text `reason` into its audit row; the Fable review removed it (below); (f) the live tokens of a closed account stay, because no operation redeems a token of an account that may not sign in ([07 §3.8](07-security-threat-model-and-permissions.md#38-email-verification-reset-and-invitation-tokens)), and its marketing consents stay until anonymisation clears them (AC-FR-IAM-009-3); (g) the controller ends the acting session itself, as `logOut` does, and flashes `notice = deletion_requested` into the guest session it leaves, so the `/login` visit that follows says the account is closed ([08 note 83](08-ui-ux-and-design-system.md#consistency-notes-for-editor)); a flash is allowed session state ([07 §3.2](07-security-threat-model-and-permissions.md#32-what-a-session-may-contain)). Limiters: `requestAccountDeletion` needs no row of its own for its email: it succeeds once per deactivation and the session it came from ends with it, so a second email needs a staff reinstatement, and its wrong passwords are bounded by `reauth`. Tests: `T-IAM-007` and `T-IAM-008` (new), `T-IAM-103`, `T-IAM-110`, `T-SEC-003`, `T-SEC-010`, `T-SEC-011`, `T-SEC-102` and `T-NOT-101` ([10 note 79](10-testing-and-quality-gates.md#consistency-notes-for-editor)). After the Fable review (2026-11-23): (1) `updateMe` was bounded by nothing, and each consent toggle adds a row to the insert-only `audit_logs`; it now takes a point of `profile_update` (20 per hour per user, proposed) on every call, and `api_user` and `api_staff` are built as the router-stack middleware `api_limits_middleware.ts`, which charges every other authenticated `/api/v1` call and skips the operations another row names and `logOut` (§9.1); (2) the free-text `reason` is gone: 01 FR-IAM-009 and 02 ask for none, and a reason typed into an insert-only audit row, which outlives anonymisation and which no role can delete, could hold a name, an address or a number the writer's masking does not catch, so the request now takes the password only and `reason` is an unknown member; (3) `full_name` and both consents sent as `null` (or `""`, which the body parser makes `null`) answer 422 `required`, because VineJS's `optional()` reads `null` as missing; `phone: ""` removes the number, as `null` does, since the two cannot be told apart once parsed; (4) the 403 `ACCOUNT_SUSPENDED` `detail` reads "This account is suspended or closed." (§5.2), because a closed account gets the same code (AC-FR-IAM-003-4); (5) a changed or removed phone clears `phone_verified_at`; (6) §7.7 says why neither operation is ⚷.
61. **The address book and the location cascades built (2026-11-23, M1 part 6b).** The `listProvinces`, `listDistricts` and `listLocalLevels` rows of §13.2 and the `listAddresses`, `createAddress`, `updateAddress` and `deleteAddress` rows of §13.4 are built and leave `x-pending-operations` for `paths` in `openapi.yaml` (its note 52); §9.1's `catalog_ip` row is built for the cascades, and §2.4 says where it runs. Decisions where the rows were short or silent, each following its owner: (a) the single-address bodies follow §3.4's envelope: `createAddress` answers 201 `{data: …}` without `Location`, because no read operation serves one address (§3.7), and `updateAddress` 200 `{data: …}`; (b) an address is the transformer's 15 members: `id`, `label`, `recipient_name`, `recipient_phone_last4`, each of the three codes with the English name of the saved unit from the reference data, active or not ([04a §9](04a-data-dictionary-tables.md#9-logistics-and-locations) "Changes"; the code stands in for a name the data does not have), `ward_no`, `area_tole`, `street_landmark`, the generated `postal_code` and `is_default`; the phone is its last four digits after a write too, as in the list (AC-FR-IAM-012-5), and only the customer address transformer of [07 §5.5](07-security-threat-model-and-permissions.md#55-encryption) decrypts the rest; (c) `updateAddress` takes every member as optional: `label` and `street_landmark` may be `null`, which clears them, and the others answer 422 `required` when sent as `null` or `""`, as `updateMe` does; the place members sent are laid over the saved ones and the whole chain is checked again with its ward, while an edit without a place member keeps a saved unit that has since become inactive (04a §9 "Changes"); `is_default: false` on an address that is not the default changes nothing; (d) the 422 item codes are `location_mismatch` on `local_level_code`, `ward_out_of_range` on `ward_no` and `default_required` on `is_default`, the codes the §13.8 pickup-address rows already use, and `address_limit` with `field` `null` for the 10-address cap [Assumption, AC-FR-IAM-012-4], checked after the place; §5.1 names item codes by example only, so the operations in `openapi.yaml` name these four; (e) `deleteAddress` takes no body member (`unknown_field`), and a repeat answers 404; (f) neither write is ⟳, because `user_addresses` has no `version` ([04 §2.10](04-domain-model-and-data-dictionary.md#210-optimistic-concurrency)), nor ⚷, since §7.7 does not list them: a repeated create adds a second address the user can remove, and a repeated edit sets the same values; each write locks the user's row first ([04a §5.5](04a-data-dictionary-tables.md#55-user_addresses)) and compares the status and stamp read under the lock with what the account check compared, so a suspension or stamp rotation that committed after the check wins (403 `ACCOUNT_SUSPENDED`, else 401 `UNAUTHENTICATED`), as for `updateMe`; no write has an audit row, because [04a §15.3](04a-data-dictionary-tables.md#153-audit_logs) lists no address action; (g) another user's, an archived or a missing address answers the same 404, and so does an `addressId` that is not a UUID, which no route matches (T-SEC-006); (h) the cascades offer only active units, provinces by code and districts and local levels by English name; a missing, repeated or malformed code, or any other parameter, is 400 `INVALID_QUERY_PARAMETER` with one `invalid` item (§6.3), and a well-formed code that names no active unit answers 200 with an empty list; (i) the cascades are charged `catalog_ip` per client network whether or not a user is signed in, and not `api_user`, because a per-user key would not bound guests; the address operations are charged `api_user`. Two points where the code and this document differed, settled by the tech lead on 2026-11-23: the four lists answer `{data: [...]}` without `meta` and take no `cursor` or `limit`, because each is bounded (7 provinces, a province's districts, a district's local levels, 10 addresses), so §6.2 gains "Bounded lists", which names them, and §3.4 points to it, where both had given every list a `meta` and a cursor (`T-API-008` checks the paged lists, [10](10-testing-and-quality-gates.md#6-test-id-registry)); and `listAddresses`, which read no query parameter, now refuses any with 400 `INVALID_QUERY_PARAMETER`, as §6.3 asks. After the Fable review, the three writes refuse any query parameter the same way, because their validator reads the body and the query merged, so a member could otherwise arrive in the query string; and a guest's `updateAddress` or `deleteAddress` with an `addressId` that is not a UUID answers 404 before the 401, because no route matches it.
62. **Single-seller launch (2026-11-23).** §13.4 says, after its table, what the product owner's decisions for R1-S change ([risks §2.3](risks-and-open-decisions.md#23-decision-log)): a guest path for `quoteCheckout` and `placeOrder`, a guest key for the `place_order` limiter, the live NCM rate as the delivery fee, and a public order lookup (proposed). No row or schema changes here, so `openapi.yaml` is unchanged; both change together with launch parts 4 and 5 ([12 §9](12-roadmap-and-backlog.md#9-single-seller-launch-r1-s)).
63. **The seller's shop reads built (2026-11-23, R1-S part 1a).** The `listMyShops` and `getSellerShop` rows of §13.5 are built and leave `x-pending-operations` for `paths` in `openapi.yaml` (its note 53). Decisions where the rows were short or silent, each following its owner: (a) `listMyShops` answers `{data: [...]}` by shop name, each row `slug`, `name`, `status` and the caller's `role`, the rows `getMe` already lists and the `seller_shops` shared prop sends ([03 §6.3](03-system-architecture.md#63-dashboards-assessment-seller-and-admin)); owned shops in every status, memberships only while `active`; no shop ID. It has no `meta` or cursor: §6.2 "Bounded lists" names it, with a bound of 20 rows (A-63). (b) `getSellerShop` answers `{data: {...}}` with a closed member list: the profile columns of [04a §6.1](04a-data-dictionary-tables.md#61-shops) that exist today, the contact phone in E.164, and `agreement` (`version`, `is_final`, `accepted`), which is how the row's "agreement status" is built: whether the shop holds a [04a §6.4](04a-data-dictionary-tables.md#64-shop_agreements) row for the current version. The logo and banner members come with FR-MED-003 (launch part 2). (c) The row named only the grievance contact as owner-only; 01 AC-FR-SHOP-013-4, which owns the rule, makes every business detail of AC-FR-SHOP-013-2 visible to the owner and reviewing staff only, so the business type, the registration number and authority, the PAN/VAT number, the VAT flag and the return policy travel in `business_details`, which is `null` for every member but the owner, like `grievance_contact`. (d) The status gate is the `shop.member` rule of [07 §4.4](07-security-threat-model-and-permissions.md#44-status-gating) (proposed, OD-48): open in `active` and both suspension modes, owner only in `pending_review` and `rejected`, refused in `closed` with 403 `SHOP_NOT_ACTIVE`; the error column says so. (e) Both refuse any query parameter (§6.3) and are charged to `api_user`. Tests: `T-SHOP-008` (new), `T-SEC-001`, `T-SEC-031` and `T-SEC-034` ([10 §6](10-testing-and-quality-gates.md#6-test-id-registry)). After the Fable review (round 2): (c) first kept the business type, the VAT flag and the return policy visible to members, narrowing AC-FR-SHOP-013-4; following its owner, all six are now in `business_details`, and [12 §9](12-roadmap-and-backlog.md#9-single-seller-launch-r1-s) part 3 reconciles the return policy's public display (FR-SHOP-003, FR-CAT-012) with the rule; `listMyShops` is capped at 20 rows (A-63) instead of being an exception to the bounded-list rule.
64. **The shop profile edit built (2026-11-23, R1-S part 1b).** The `updateShopProfile` row of §13.5 is built and leaves `x-pending-operations` for `paths` in `openapi.yaml` (its note 54); §9.1 adds the `shop_profile_update` limiter (proposed). Decisions where the row was short or silent, each following its owner: (a) **Owner-only members** (decided 2026-11-23 for R1-S part 1b). 01 AC-FR-SHOP-013-4 shows every business detail of AC-FR-SHOP-013-2 to the owner and reviewing staff only, and `getSellerShop` gives them to the owner only (note 63 (c)), so the business type, the registration number and authority, the PAN/VAT number, the VAT flag and the return policy are written by the owner only, like the grievance contact the row already named. A member with `profile.manage` who is not the owner edits the description and the shop's contact; an owner-only member from them answers 403 `FORBIDDEN` and nothing is written. In R1-S the owner is the only member (staff invitations wait), so this restricts nobody yet; whether storefront pages show the return policy stays the part 3 question of [12 §9](12-roadmap-and-backlog.md#9-single-seller-launch-r1-s). (b) **Members.** Flat and named as `getSellerShop` names them (`registration_number`, not the column's `business_registration_number`; the grievance contact as `grievance_contact_name` and `grievance_contact_phone`), each optional; an absent member keeps its column. `null` (or `""`, which the body parser reads as `null`) clears the description, the registration number and authority and the PAN/VAT number within the rules of (c), and is 422 `required` for every other member. The rules are those of `platform:create-shop` ([09 §9.8](09-code-structure-and-engineering-standards.md#98-the-owners-shop-node-ace-platformcreate-shop-proposed)): both numbers a Nepali mobile or landline stored in E.164 (AC-FR-SHOP-001-3), the account email rule, lengths in code points after NFC, the PAN/VAT number as 9 digits (VX-05). (c) **Business details on an approved shop.** [12 §9](12-roadmap-and-backlog.md#9-single-seller-launch-r1-s) part 1 enters the AC-FR-SHOP-013-2 details in the profile, while the multi-vendor flow takes them at application, where staff review them (TM-31), and AC-FR-SHOP-003-1 does not list them. In R1-S the owner changes them directly in every status the gate allows, audited, and the CHECKs of [04a §6.1](04a-data-dictionary-tables.md#61-shops) are checked on the result before the database would refuse it: a `registered_business` needs its registration number, registering authority and PAN/VAT number, and a VAT-registered shop its PAN/VAT number, else 422 `required` on the missing member; an individual's PAN/VAT number is neither required nor refused while OD-16 and VX-05 are open. Whether an approved vendor may change them the same way, or only through review or staff, is the new [OD-64](risks-and-open-decisions.md#22-decision-table), which blocks M2 code and not R1-S. (d) **No listing refresh.** No member changes the shop's name: AC-FR-SHOP-003-1 does not list it, 04a §6.1 sets it when the shop is created, and staff change only the slug (FR-SHOP-012). The row's side effect "listing refresh if name changes" could never fire and is removed; an operation that renames a shop, if one is added, sends `catalog.refresh_listing` for the shop's products, which launch part 2 builds. (e) **Order of the checks.** The permission, the status gate (the "profile, shipping" column of 07 §4.4, `shopGateAllows(shop, 'profile')`), the members (an unknown one 422 `unknown_field`, an owner-only one from a non-owner 403, a forbidden `null` 422), the validator, then `If-Match` (428). The action locks the shop row `FOR NO KEY UPDATE` (level 0 of [05 §4.4](05-order-payment-and-inventory-lifecycles.md#44-global-lock-ordering)), checks the gate again on the locked status, so a suspension committed after `seller_context` read the shop wins with 403, then the version (412 with `current` through `getSellerShop`'s transformer for the caller, so a manager's `current` has no business details), then the rules of (c). The write is a compare-and-set on `version` and the locked status. A request that changes nothing writes nothing and keeps the version and ETag; the grievance phone counts as changed whenever it is sent, because the action is not on the decryption allowlist of [07 §5.5](07-security-threat-model-and-permissions.md#55-encryption). (f) **Audit and encryption.** One `shop.profile_update` row (proposed, [04a §15.3](04a-data-dictionary-tables.md#153-audit_logs)) for each request that changes something: `changed` names the written columns, and only `business_type` and `is_vat_registered` carry their from and to values. Every other column goes by name only: the grievance contact and an individual's identifiers are personal, and the audit writer refuses any string that holds an email address or a mobile number, which the shop's public contact, the description and the return policy may hold (T-SEC-102). The grievance phone is encrypted before the transaction with the AAD `shops.grievance_contact_phone_enc`; 04a §6.1 gives it no blind index, so none is written. (g) **Limiter.** `shop_profile_update` (proposed), 20 per hour per user, as `profile_update` is for `updateMe`, because each change adds an audit row kept 7 years. (h) **Out of 1b.** The logo and banner media IDs (FR-MED-003, with launch part 2's media pipeline), `pickup_address` and `return_address` (pickup addresses have their own operations since the courier work, and 1c shows them on `/shipping`) and `shop_category_codes` (the owner's shop has no category assignment, and nothing reads one before the public shop page, FR-SRCH-003, which waits) stay in the row as later members; sending one now answers 422 `unknown_field`. Tests: `T-SHOP-009` (new), `T-API-004`, `T-SEC-001`, `T-SEC-003`, `T-SEC-011`, `T-SEC-030`, `T-SEC-031`, `T-SEC-034` and `T-SEC-102` ([10 §6](10-testing-and-quality-gates.md#6-test-id-registry)). After the Fable review (round 2): (g) the limiter is charged first, in the API limits middleware (`USER_LIMIT_OPERATIONS`), before the route's middleware and every check, so a refused call (403, 404, 422, 428) takes a point and a loop of them meets 429, as the login limiters charge before their check (§9.1); follow-up: `updateMe`'s `profile_update` is still taken inside its action, after the validator, so its refused calls may cost nothing, and it can move to the same map. (b) A value of spaces clears `description`, `registration_number`, `registration_authority` and `pan_vat_number` as `""` does (§3.5: strings are trimmed and an empty string becomes `null`) instead of answering `min_length`; the address book's optional members still refuse it. `openapi.yaml` gains the validator's `minLength` on the registration number and authority. The settings page moves focus to the conflict panel when a 412 shows it and to the save button when it closes, restarts the form from the 200 body (so a failed props reload cannot leave a stale version) and lists a 422 on a field it does not show in the error summary (08 note 87).
65. **The shop's shipping built (2026-11-23, R1-S part 1c).** The `getShopShipping` and `replaceShopShipping` rows of §13.5 are built and leave `x-pending-operations` for `paths` in `openapi.yaml` (its note 55). Decisions where the rows were short, each following its owner: (a) **Shape.** `getShopShipping` answers `{data: {coverage, rates, configured, version}}` (§3.4): the covered district codes, one rate per zone with the fee as Money (§3.3) and the delivery estimate, `configured`, the publish gate's "shipping is configured" condition (01 AC-FR-CAT-005-2, AC-FR-SHOP-004-3), so part 2's gate and the overview's "Shipping zones and rates set" item read one rule (`shippingConfigured` in `app/modules/logistics/queries.ts`), and `version`, `shops.version`, as §8 names it. Both operations refuse a query parameter (400). (b) **Each set replaced whole, an absent one kept.** The row named `coverage[]` and `rates[]` without saying whether both are required. The `PUT` replaces each set it carries whole and keeps an absent one, so the shipping form sends only the set it changed (08 §7.1) and a "Keep my changes" after a 412 cannot overwrite the other set unseen; it is still a whole-set replacement in the sense of §3.1, per set. A request that changes nothing writes nothing and keeps the version. (c) **Rules.** From 01 AC-FR-SHOP-004-1 and 04a §9.6, §9.7: at least one covered district; a fee of 0 or more paisa, a JSON integer; estimates of whole days from 0 to 30 with the fastest no longer than the slowest; on the result, every covered district's zone has a rate (05 §3.3 item 3, `T-SHOP-109`). A rate for a zone the shop does not cover is kept, because it prices nothing until the shop covers a district there and the zone rate is A-61's fallback fee. A district or zone that is not active answers 422 `not_offered` (proposed item code), an estimate out of order `less_than_min` and a covered zone without a rate `rate_required` (both proposed), naming the zone. (d) **Gate and concurrency.** The read follows the `shop.member` rule of §4.4 (open while suspended), the write the "profile, shipping" column (OD-47); the write locks the shop row, checks the gate and the version again on it, as `updateShopProfile` does, and both move `shops.version`, so a shipping save after a profile save is stale (412) and the reverse too. (e) **Audit.** One `shop.shipping_replace` row (proposed, [04a §15.3](04a-data-dictionary-tables.md#153-audit_logs)) with the from and to values of each set written: district and zone codes, fees in paisa and day counts, none of them personal. (f) **Limiter.** §9.1 gives neither operation a row, so both are charged to `api_user`. Follow-up: unlike the profile edit, whose `shop_profile_update` (20 an hour) bounds the audit rows it adds, a shipping save that changes something is bounded only by `api_user` (300 a minute), as the pickup-address writes are; whether they need a row of their own is not decided here. Tests: `T-SHOP-010` (new), `T-SHOP-109`, `T-API-004`, `T-SEC-001`, `T-SEC-003`, `T-SEC-030` and `T-SEC-031` ([10 §6](10-testing-and-quality-gates.md#6-test-id-registry)). After the Fable review (round 2): the rate rule and `configured` read only the covered districts the editor offers (active district, province and zone), so a saved district that is no longer offered stays in `coverage` until the next coverage save, which must leave it out (`not_offered`), and needs no rate, as a saved address keeps a retired place until it is changed ([04a §9](04a-data-dictionary-tables.md#9-logistics-and-locations) "Changes"); otherwise a zone made inactive would ask for a rate no request may send. `fee_minor` is at most 99,999,999,999 paisa (`SHIPPING_LIMITS.feeMinor`), the most the form's rupee field reads, so every saved fee loads back into the form.
66. **OD-44's own-shop check built (2026-11-24, R1-S part 1c-ii).** §4.3 adds the check the product owner decided on 2026-11-23 ([risks §2.3](risks-and-open-decisions.md#23-decision-log), [07 §4.1](07-security-threat-model-and-permissions.md#41-principles) item 4), and seven §13.8 rows name it: `adminSetLogisticsAccountStatus` (a shop-owned account only), `adminAllowShopOnLogisticsAccount`, `adminRemoveShopFromLogisticsAccount`, `adminSetShopLogisticsEnabled`, `adminResolveCourierBooking`, `adminResolveCourierEvent` and `adminRecordOrderVerification`. Each takes an optional `totp_code` and may answer 403 `FORBIDDEN`, 422 on `totp_code` and 429 `RATE_LIMITED`; `openapi.yaml` adds `OwnShopTotpCode` and `OwnShopCodeRequest` (its note 56). Decisions where the owners were silent: (a) **Which shops are their own.** The owner, or an `active` membership, in any shop status, read in the action's transaction. (b) **Which operations.** Every admin write that changes a shop's data or its orders by staff's choice. Reads, which show the owner nothing their seller area does not, and `adminRefreshCourierStatus`, which only asks the courier again as `recheckPayment` asks the provider, are not refused. A platform-owned account and a courier reading that matched no shipment are nobody's shop. (c) **No code** under the mode is 422 on `totp_code` (`required`), not 403, so a dialog can ask for the field. (d) **Order of checks.** 404 first, then the own-shop check, then the state checks, all after an idempotency key's insert: with the mode off the refusal comes before any code is read, so it charges no limiter and spends no code. (e) **The step-up operations** (`adminSetLogisticsAccountStatus` and the allow and remove pair) accept the body's code in place of a stale step-up, as §4.3's self-approval code does, on any shop; on an operation without step-up a code sent for another shop is ignored. (f) The DELETE of `adminRemoveShopFromLogisticsAccount` takes an optional JSON body with only `totp_code`. Tests: `T-SEC-045` (new, [10 §6](10-testing-and-quality-gates.md#6-test-id-registry)).
67. **The product drafts built (2026-11-24, R1-S part 2a).** The `createProduct`, `getShopProduct`, `listShopProducts` and `updateProduct` rows of §13.5 are built; the last three leave `x-pending-operations` for `paths` in `openapi.yaml` (its note 57). Decisions where the rows were short or silent: (a) **One editor shape.** `SellerProduct` gains the editor fields (`description`, `brand`, `attributes`, the disclosures, `rejection_reason`, `option_axes`, `updated_at`) and `SellerVariant` gains `status`, `compare_at_price` and `weight_grams`, so the create, read and edit answers and the editor page share one transformer, as [09 §12.9](09-code-structure-and-engineering-standards.md#129-transformer) intends. A variant's `label` is `Default`, or `Attribute: Value` per axis joined by `/`, as §14.2 shows. (b) **`updateProduct`** is partial: a member left out keeps its value, `null` clears a nullable one, and `title`, `category_id`, `attributes` and `is_imported` may not be `null` (422 `required`). `attributes`, when sent, replaces the set; when left out, the stored set is checked again, against a new category too, and a new category must allow the product's option axes (`axes_not_allowed`). Only what the request sends or changes is checked against other rows: a new category must be an active leaf, a new brand selectable, a sent origin consistent, and the attribute set is checked when it is sent or the category changes. A field left alone is not checked again, so a platform change to a rule or a brand never blocks a vendor's unrelated edit; a product that no longer complies stays as it is and is flagged later ([04 §3.7](04-domain-model-and-data-dictionary.md) "Revisit when"). A live product (`published`, `unpublished`) must keep every disclosure, and, when its attributes or category change, every required attribute and every required axis of its category (`axes_required`), as `products_disclosures_check` and 04 §3.7 rule 4 require; it may not switch to a brand with `requires_moderation`, whose products always go through review (04 §3.10, AC-FR-CAT-008-3): the vendor unpublishes it first (`moderation_required` on `brand_id`). A request that changes nothing writes nothing and keeps the version. (c) **Audit.** `product.create` (proposed) records the status and the category, and `product.update` (proposed) the names of the changed fields: never the title or other free text, which a vendor may fill with anything, including a phone number the audit writer refuses ([04a §15.3](04a-data-dictionary-tables.md#153-audit_logs)). (d) **`listShopProducts`**: without `status`, every product but the archived ones (04a §7.6); `q` is a case-insensitive title prefix or a SKU prefix of any variant, 1 to 100 characters; `variant_count` counts active variants. (e) **Gates** ([07 §4.4](07-security-threat-model-and-permissions.md#44-status-gating)): the reads are open while the shop is `active` or `suspended`, the writes while `active` only. (f) **`catalog.refresh_listing`** is sent by every write, as 09 §12.2 decision 3 says; until publishing exists (R1-S part 2e) its handler only removes the row of a product that is not visible. Tests: `T-CAT-008`, `T-CAT-009` and `T-CAT-010` (new), with `T-CAT-001`, `T-CAT-002`, `T-CAT-007`, `T-CAT-101`, `T-CAT-104`, `T-CAT-105`, `T-CAT-108` (in part), `T-API-003`, `T-API-004`, `T-API-007`, `T-SEC-001`, `T-SEC-003`, `T-SEC-030` and `T-SEC-031` ([10 §6](10-testing-and-quality-gates.md#6-test-id-registry)).
68. **The variants built (2026-11-24, R1-S part 2b).** The `replaceProductVariants` row of §13.5 is built; `openapi.yaml` already specified it, and its note 58 adds what the build decided. Decisions where the owners were silent, each recorded in its owner:
    - **A variant with history keeps its options** ([04a §7.8](04a-data-dictionary-tables.md#78-product_option_axes), [§7.9](04a-data-dictionary-tables.md#79-product_variants)): it may be repriced, given another SKU, archived or re-activated, but its option values never change, because its stock and order lines describe that combination (422 `history`).
    - **Fates and write order** ([04a §7.9](04a-data-dictionary-tables.md#79-product_variants) "Lifecycle and retention"): a variant left out without history is deleted whatever its status, one with history is archived, and the writes keep the partial unique indexes valid after every statement, so two variants may swap SKUs or options.
    - **Axes**: an axis the product already has stays usable after the platform drops its rule; a new axis must be an effective `variant_axis` rule (`not_allowed`).
    - **Live products** keep every required axis (`required` on `option_axes`, 04 §3.7 rule 4), at least one variant and a price above zero on each (AC-FR-CAT-004-3).
    - **Locks**: the product row, then its variants' stock rows (level 7 of [05 §4.4](05-order-payment-and-inventory-lifecycles.md#44-global-lock-ordering), in `variant_id` order), then the history check, so a stock adjustment either commits first and its variant is archived, or waits.
    - **Audit** `product.variants_replace` (proposed, [04a §15.3](04a-data-dictionary-tables.md#153-audit_logs)) records the axes and the counts, never a SKU. A variant `id` is compared in lower case.

    Tests: `T-CAT-011` (new), `T-CAT-102`, `T-CAT-103`, `T-CAT-106`, `T-CAT-109`, `T-API-004`, `T-SEC-001` (case (c)) and `T-SEC-003` ([10 §6](10-testing-and-quality-gates.md#6-test-id-registry)).

69. **The stock built (2026-11-24, R1-S part 2c).** The `listInventory`, `adjustInventory` and `stocktakeInventory` rows of §13.5 are built; `openapi.yaml` specified the two writes, specifies `listInventory` now, and its note 59 adds what the build decided. Decisions where the owners were silent, each recorded in its owner:
    - **Lock, then the guarded update** ([05 §5.9](05-order-payment-and-inventory-lifecycles.md#59-adjustments-and-stocktake)): the action reads the stock row `FOR UPDATE` inside the shop's scope, then runs the conditional update, so the refusal is decided on the row it holds and the audit row gets `on_hand` before the change. No row is 404 (T-SEC-001).
    - **Refusals**: a result below zero with nothing reserved is the same 409 `below_reserved`; one above the `int` column's limit is 422 `max` on `delta`; a `delta` of 0 is 422 `not_zero`. A stale `expected_on_hand`, higher or lower, is `stock_changed` before any `below_reserved`. `committed_shop_orders` lists at most 20 numbers, oldest first (§5.1, [05 §8.13](05-order-payment-and-inventory-lifecycles.md#813-stock-adjusted-below-reserved)). A refused request stores no key. An omitted, null or blank `note` is one request for the key's fingerprint (§7.2). An archived variant's stock may still be changed, by its ID.
    - **Side effects**: the movement references the idempotency key row (`reference_type = 'request'`, [04a §8.3](04a-data-dictionary-tables.md#83-inventory_movements)); one `inventory.adjust` or `inventory.stocktake` audit row with `on_hand` from and to, the reason and the movement, never the note ([04a §15.3](04a-data-dictionary-tables.md#153-audit_logs) "Stock events"); `catalog.refresh_listing`, for a count only when `on_hand` changed.
    - **The list**: one item per product with the product list's filters, order and cursor (§6.3), each with its active variants' SKU, label, stock and latest movement. `low_stock` is R2, so in R1 it is an unknown parameter (400). The movement history of 02 J-11 step 4 is a page prop of the inventory page, built with the seller pages (R1-S part 2f).

    Tests: `T-INV-008` and `T-INV-009` (new), `T-INV-002`, `T-SEC-001`, `T-SEC-003`, `T-SEC-030`, `T-SEC-031` and the reverse race of `T-CAT-106` ([10 §6](10-testing-and-quality-gates.md#6-test-id-registry)).

70. **The uploads built (2026-11-24, R1-S part 2d-i).** The `createMediaUpload` and `completeMediaUpload` rows of §13.5 are built; `openapi.yaml` specifies them now (its note 60). Decisions where the owners were silent or disagreed, each recorded in its owner:
    - **Kinds**: R1-S offers `product_image` only, under `shop.products.edit` and the "products edit, publish; inventory" gate ([07 §4.8](07-security-threat-model-and-permissions.md#48-how-policies-are-implemented)). Logo and banner (FR-MED-003, if wanted) and KYC documents with `document_type` join with their features ([12 §9](12-roadmap-and-backlog.md#9-single-seller-launch-r1-s)).
    - **A declared size above 10 MB** is 422 `VALIDATION_FAILED` on `bytes` (`max`), as §9.2 says, not 413: 02 J-10 is corrected.
    - **Signing comes first**: the URL is presigned for a new UUIDv7 before the row is inserted, so a store that cannot sign answers 503 `PROVIDER_UNAVAILABLE` and leaves no row ([03 §7.5](03-system-architecture.md#75-media-upload-pipeline-j-10-fr-med-001-adr-0013) is corrected).
    - **The finish** answers 202 `processing` for an object of the declared type, storing its ETag and its stored size, which may differ from the declared `bytes` (that stays as declared; the worker reads the stored object); 200 `rejected` with a reason the seller sees, for an empty object, one above 10 MB, one whose `Content-Type` differs from the declared mime, or one whose ETag the column cannot hold, which is then deleted (best effort); 409 `CONFLICT` with an `upload_missing` item (§5.1) when no object has arrived, writing nothing so the seller may PUT again and finish once more; and 503 when the store cannot be asked.
    - **No audit row** for an upload: nothing a buyer sees changes until `replaceProductMedia` uses the asset.

    Tests: `T-MED-004` (new), `T-ARCH-003` (its storage case), `T-ARCH-024`, `T-SEC-001`, `T-SEC-003`, `T-SEC-030`, `T-SEC-031` ([10 §6](10-testing-and-quality-gates.md#6-test-id-registry)).

71. **The gallery built (2026-11-26, R1-S part 2d-iii).** §13.5's `replaceProductMedia` row records the build: positions 1 to n (so position 1 is the primary image), an asset at most once, a colour of an active variant, at least one image on a live product (`published` or `unpublished`; a draft may have none), the no-op rule, the audit action `product.media_replace` (proposed) and the listing refresh; the answer is the whole editor product, so the row's response reads "Product with media" as `replaceProductVariants` does. `openapi.yaml` moves the operation from `x-pending-operations` to `paths` (its note 61). Tests: `T-MED-006` (new), `T-MED-101`, `T-MED-102`, `T-SEC-001`, `T-SEC-003`, `T-SEC-030`, `T-SEC-031` ([10 note 92](10-testing-and-quality-gates.md#consistency-notes-for-editor)).
72. **The publish lifecycle built (2026-11-26, R1-S part 2e-ii).** §13.5's `publishProduct`, `unpublishProduct`, `archiveProduct` and `restoreProduct` rows record the build: a compare-and-set on `status` and `version`, the version bumped; 409 with `allowed_events` for a move the status does not allow (a draft allows only `publish`; `pending_review`, `rejected` and `blocked` allow none of the four); no query parameter and no body member. The publication gate's 422 lists every missing item under code `required` (`agreement`, `variants`, `media`, the disclosures, `attributes`, `option_axes`, `shipping`), and a rule that fails under its own code. Decided in the build: the agreement item accepts any version the platform still accepts (AC-FR-SHOP-013-3); a draft is also checked as a new product is (an active leaf category, an `active` brand), while an unpublished product keeps its category and brand; the review-mode and watch-listed-brand 409 applies to drafts only; an attribute problem is given on `attributes` without an index, its message naming the attribute. `updateProduct`'s `moderation_required` message now names archive and restore, since an unpublished product is refused too (note 67 said unpublish). `openapi.yaml` moves the four from `x-pending-operations` to `paths` (its note 62). Tests: `T-CAT-013` (new), `T-SEC-001`, `T-SEC-003`, `T-SEC-030`, `T-SEC-031` ([10 note 94](10-testing-and-quality-gates.md#consistency-notes-for-editor)).
73. **The storefront's reference reads built (2026-11-26, R1-S part 3a).** §13.2's `listCategories` and `listAttributes` rows record the build, §6.2 lists both as bounded lists, and §2.4 and §9.1 put them on `catalog_ip`. The category tree leaves out an active category under an inactive parent, as the listing never shows it. Decided in the build: with `category`, `listAttributes` answers the filterable attributes a rule on that category, an ancestor or a listed descendant names, not the ancestors' alone as the row said, because the listing shows the whole subtree: `clothing` offers the sizes its leaves vary by. A rule counts only on a listed category (active, every ancestor active), so a hidden subtree adds no filter. A well-formed slug of no listed category answers an empty list, as the location cascades do for a code of no unit. 04a §7.1's per-process cache of the tree is not built: each call reads the database, behind `catalog_ip` ([04 note 57](04-domain-model-and-data-dictionary.md#consistency-notes-for-editor)). `openapi.yaml` moves both from `x-pending-operations` to `paths` (its note 63). Tests: `T-CAT-015` (new) and `T-CAT-107` ([10 note 98](10-testing-and-quality-gates.md#consistency-notes-for-editor)).
